definitions.explanation: Small, round dumplings made from rice flour, often served on skewers.

examples.english: Dumplings over flowers. (Proverb: Practical things over aesthetic pleasures)
examples.notes: Famous proverb meaning practicality over beauty

examples.japanese: みたらし{団子|だんご}を{三本|さんぼん}{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought three mitarashi dango skewers.

examples.japanese: {月見|つきみ}{団子|だんご}を{供|そな}える。
examples.notes: Tradition during the autumn moon festival

notes:
A traditional Japanese sweet made from rice flour (上新粉/白玉粉). Common types:
- みたらし{団子|だんご} (with sweet soy glaze)
- {三色|さんしょく}{団子|だんご}/{花見|はなみ}{団子|だんご} (tri-color: pink, white, green)
- {月見|つきみ}{団子|だんご} (plain white, for moon viewing)
- あんこ{団子|だんご} (with sweet bean paste)
- {草|くさ}{団子|だんご} (with mugwort)
- ごま{団子|だんご} (with sesame)

Typically served on skewers ({串|くし}). The proverb 「{花|はな}より{団子|だんご}」 reflects the Japanese appreciation for practicality.

Counted: {一本|いっぽん} (per skewer) or {一個|いっこ} (individual dumpling).
